column3: “Chamber of the beds” is rendered “bedroom,” and NASB supplies “placed.”
“Runners” is rendered “guard,” and “made to swear” as “put them under oath.”
NASB continues the sentence into verse 6.
NASB puts the first part in parentheses; “by turns” (Hebrew מַסָּח) is rendered “for defense,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“Two hands” is rendered “two parts,” and NASB adds “even” and “also.”
“Runners” is rendered “guards,” and “south … north” as “right … left.”
NASB supplies “gave him” for the testimony; “struck a palm” is rendered “clapped their hands.”
“The runners, the people” is rendered “the guard and … the people.”
“Officers of the army” is rendered “who were appointed over the army.”
“They put hands to her” is rendered “they seized her.”
